subject: literature
passage: Señor Ibarra had closed his tailor shop in Buenos Aires years ago, and he told anyone who asked that he did not miss it. So when his granddaughter brought him her torn winter coat, he grumbled that she should simply buy another. Still, he turned the coat over in his hands, studying the seam. By evening he had found his old spool of gray thread, cleared the kitchen table, and bent over the work, humming a tune she had not heard him hum in years.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: A retired tailor who claims not to miss his work seems to enjoy returning to it.
choices.B: A grandfather refuses to mend his granddaughter's coat because he has retired.
choices.C: A retired tailor regrets closing his shop and decides to open it once again.
choices.D: A granddaughter tears her winter coat and asks her grandfather to repair it.

explanation.why: Ibarra says he does not miss tailoring and grumbles about the coat, but his actions tell a different story: he studies the seam, finds his old thread, and works while "humming a tune she had not heard him hum in years." The main idea is the contrast between what he claims and the pleasure he shows.
explanation.A: Correct. This captures the contrast at the heart of the passage: his claim not to miss the work versus his evident pleasure in doing it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. He grumbles at first, but by evening he is mending the coat.
explanation.C: Incorrect. He enjoys one repair job, but nothing suggests he regrets closing the shop or plans to reopen it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is only the event that starts the passage; it leaves out how Ibarra responds.
